name: Vivian Acosta
life: “I still remember an officer sharing my dripping shop awning.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Vivian by a small Wednesday habit. Vivian checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I came to complain about my street and held an umbrella over the officer I was going to name.
appearance: Vivian is easy to recognize by dark brown curls cut close behind the ears and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a narrow-striped sweater with a train token tied to a zipper pull, Vivian starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Vivian enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Vivian is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To deliver the complaint to the officer who shared the umbrella.
family: Duncan Stahl is Vivian’s half-sibling. Vivian makes the call. Duncan is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Duncan says, “I agreed to show my nails. Nobody asked whether my accident was part of the product.”
connections: Adrian Bhandari. They arrange two private ways to finish a complaint after the storm.
